extracted.intended_audience: novelists, aspiring fiction writers, critics and students of fiction
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on choosing and executing narrative method (scenic/dramatic vs pictorial/expository) in novels — how to prepare effects, create a sense of time, manage point of view, and economize the climax. Uses Balzac and Tolstoy as contrasting exemplars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare effect with a preliminary pictorial picture
rubrics_metrics.description: His preliminary picture included the representation of time, secured the sense of it so thoroughly that there is no necessity for recurring to it again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a rich, enduring impression of setting and routine early on (as Balzac does for the Maison Grandet) so that later passage of years or change can be implied briefly (e.g. 'Five years went by') rather than repeatedly dramatized. Build latent character traits in the scene so later events feel inevitable without prolonged interior elaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convey the passage of time by establishing routine and environment
rubrics_metrics.description: The routine of the Maison Grandet is too clearly known to be forgotten; the sight of the girl and her mother... Their dreary days accumulate and fill the year with hardly a break in its monotony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To show long-term change or decay, render the continuity and sameness of a life through external, repeatable details (household routine, accumulation/loss of possessions) rather than only by prolonging the protagonist's inner monologue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of climax — do not overload the climax
rubrics_metrics.description: The climax ought to complete, to add the touch that makes the book whole and organic; that is its task, and that only... He saves his climax, in other words, from the burden of deliberate expatiation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve what the climax must accomplish by preparing it beforehand; ensure the climax only provides the necessary final movement. Avoid making the climax responsible for exposition or for carrying effects that could have been prepared earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invisible preparation — do not betray the art of preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: The art of preparation is no art if it betrays itself at the outset... By definition it is unrecognizable until it attains its end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreshadow and reserve effects subtly. Preparation should not call attention to itself or feel like deliberate padding—its success lies in the reader perceiving the completed effect without noticing the mechanics that produced it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose point of view to suit the subject and character depth
rubrics_metrics.description: To Eugénie ‘the great and only adventure of her life was contained in the few days or weeks of Charles’s first visit... It is much better to look at it from outside, as Balzac does for the most part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a character lacks deep inner complexity or 'the stuff of character' to sustain long interior study, prefer external/pictorial presentation rather than prolonged intimate POV. Conversely, if inner life is rich and needs gradual revelation, use interior access more freely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenic/dramatic presentation — show in scenes with exact time/place
rubrics_metrics.description: The whole of the book, very nearly, is scenic... On every page the hour and the place are exactly defined. Something is happening there, or something is being discussed; at any rate it is an episode singled out for direct vision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use chains of precise, staged scenes (dialogue, action, defined moments) to create immediacy. This method excels at making actions and moments vivid and at revealing character through behaviour, but it requires space and may delay generalizing or summarizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condense and tightly pack the given situation when crisis arrives early
rubrics_metrics.description: If the situation is to be really made and constituted, the space it may cover must be tightly packed; the method should be that which most condenses and concentrates the representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a story's critical turning-point occurs at or near the start (so the book must begin at a height), the author must compress background and character efficiently — either by concentrated pictorial set-up or by exceptionally economical scenic writing — so that later actions are intelligible and not arbitrary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match narrative method to the subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The method of the book, in short, does not arise out of the subject; in treating it Tolstoy simply used the method that was congenial to him, without regarding the story that he had to tell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select scenic/dramatic or pictorial/expository approaches according to what the story requires. Do not impose a favored method on a subject that needs the opposite treatment; mismatches can produce flaws (e.g. inadequate preparation for a major crisis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use repetition against a changing scene to intensify effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Each time his researches are on the verge of yielding him the 'absolute'... instead of losing force (for the onlooker) by repetition, are renewed and increased by the sight of the spreading devastation around him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a story requires reiteration of a single effect (obsession, failure), stage each repetition against progressively altered outward circumstances so that the cumulative effect grows rather than tires the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible access to consciousness — mix scenic presentation with interior glimpses
rubrics_metrics.description: He never hesitates to lay bare the mind of any of his people, at any moment, if it seems to help the force or the lucidity of the scene... a mixed method which enables Tolstoy to deal with his immense subject on the lines of drama.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feel free to move between dramatic scenes and occasional interior revelation when it clarifies motive or intensifies a scene, but be mindful of possible confusion; use interior access sparingly and purposively to augment dramatic vision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create character quickly through vivid, concentrated small scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: He can create a character in so few words — he can make the manner of a man's or a woman's thought so quickly intelligible — that even though his story is crowded... he can render them all, so to speak, by the way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ brief, evocative vignettes or half-page moments that illuminate a character's temperament or habitual response; such concentrated scenes can supply resonance and make characters 'complete' with economies of space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure actions are grounded so they are not arbitrary
rubrics_metrics.description: Without this her action is arbitrary and meaningless; it is vain to say that she acted thus and thus unless we perfectly understand what she was, what she had, what was around her...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize rendering the past, environment, and inner constitution that explain why a character chooses as they do. Readers must be given enough of the character's life and circumstances to judge the plausibility and weight of pivotal decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipation and reservation — write pages in service of later pages
rubrics_metrics.description: The process of writing a novel seems to be one of continual forestalling and anticipating; far more important than the immediate page is the page to come, still in the distance, on behalf of which this one is secretly working.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan and write so that earlier passages plant, reserve, and quietly supply effects for later scenes. Each page should contribute—often by implication—to outcomes to be realized later, without drawing attention to its preparatory role.
